questions.knowledgeNote: AP gives ratio 1 (written x/x), GP gives x/y via y^2 = xz, HP gives x/z via y = 2xz/(x+z): one computation, three readings.
questions.question: Q1(a). Prove that x, y, z are in A.P., G.P. or H.P. according as (x-y)/(y-z) = x/x or x/y or x/z respectively.
questions.solution: A.P.: (x-y)/(y-z) = x/x = 1 gives x-y = y-z, i.e. 2y = x+z, the A.P. condition. G.P.: (x-y)/(y-z) = x/y gives xy-y^2 = xy-xz, i.e. y^2 = xz, the G.P. condition. H.P.: (x-y)/(y-z) = x/z gives xz-yz = xy-xz, i.e. 2xz = y(x+z), so y = 2xz/(x+z), the H.P. condition. Each step reverses, so the three cases are proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q1(a); book p214 = PDF p241 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Clear the HP condition 2/y = 2/(x+y) + 2/(y+z): everything cancels except xz = y^2.
questions.question: Q1(b). If (x+y)/2, y and (y+z)/2 are in H.P., show that x, y, z are in G.P.
questions.solution: The three means are in H.P., so 2/y = 1/((x+y)/2) + 1/((y+z)/2) = 2/(x+y) + 2/(y+z). Dividing by 2: 1/y = (y+z+x+y)/((x+y)(y+z)) = (x+z+2y)/((x+y)(y+z)). Cross-multiplying: (x+y)(y+z) = y(x+z+2y), i.e. xy+xz+y^2+yz = xy+xz+2y^2, so y^2 = xz. Hence x, y, z are in G.P.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q1(b); book p214 = PDF p241 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitute G^2 = ab first: the two fractions combine over ab(b-a) and the (b-a) cancels.
questions.question: Q1(c). If G is the geometric mean between a and b, show that 1/(G^2-a^2) + 1/(G^2-b^2) = 1/G^2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q1(c); book p214 = PDF p241 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Write H = 2ab/(a+b), then 2H-(a+b) = -(a-b)^2/(a+b): the square cancels against the denominator.
questions.question: Q2(a). If H is the harmonic mean between a and b, prove that 1/(H-a) + 1/(H-b) = 1/a + 1/b.
questions.solution: H = 2ab/(a+b). Now 1/(H-a) + 1/(H-b) = (2H-a-b)/((H-a)(H-b)). The numerator: 2H-(a+b) = 4ab/(a+b)-(a+b) = (4ab-(a+b)^2)/(a+b) = -(a-b)^2/(a+b). The denominator: (H-a)(H-b) = H^2-H(a+b)+ab = 4a^2b^2/(a+b)^2-2ab+ab = -ab(a-b)^2/(a+b)^2. Dividing: (-(a-b)^2/(a+b))/(-ab(a-b)^2/(a+b)^2) = (a+b)/ab = 1/a+1/b.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q2(a); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: a-A = (a-b)/2 but a-H = a(a-b)/(a+b): each ratio keeps one factor (a+b), and their product is A/H.
questions.question: Q2(b). If A and H are the arithmetic and harmonic means between a and b respectively, prove that (a-A)(b-A)/((a-H)(b-H)) = A/H.
questions.solution: A = (a+b)/2, H = 2ab/(a+b). a-A = a-(a+b)/2 = (a-b)/2; a-H = a-2ab/(a+b) = a(a-b)/(a+b). So (a-A)/(a-H) = ((a-b)/2)/(a(a-b)/(a+b)) = (a+b)/(2a). Likewise (b-A)/(b-H) = (a+b)/(2b). Multiplying: (a+b)^2/(4ab). And A/H = ((a+b)/2)/(2ab/(a+b)) = (a+b)^2/(4ab). Both sides agree.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q2(b); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: These conditions force x = y = z (then the HM claim is trivial): derive 2x^2-xy-y^2 = 0, i.e. (x-y)(2x+y) = 0.
questions.question: Q3(a). If x is the A.M. between y and z, and y is the G.M. between z and x, prove that z will be the H.M. between x and y.
questions.solution: x = (y+z)/2 and y^2 = zx, so z = 2x-y. Then y^2 = x(2x-y) = 2x^2-xy, i.e. 2x^2-xy-y^2 = 0, so (x-y)(2x+y) = 0. For positive quantities x = y, hence z = 2x-y = x. So x = y = z, for which 2/z = 1/x+1/y holds (2/x = 2/x): z is indeed the H.M. between x and y.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q3(a); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: AP gives c = 2b-a; HP of b,c,a gives 2ab = c(a+b): substituting forces (a+2b)(a-b) = 0, so a = b = c.
questions.question: Q3(b). If a, b, c are in A.P., and b, c, a are in H.P., prove that c, a, b are in G.P.
questions.solution: From the A.P., 2b = a+c, so c = 2b-a. From the H.P., 2/c = 1/b+1/a = (a+b)/ab, so 2ab = c(a+b). Substituting c: 2ab = (2b-a)(a+b) = 2ab+2b^2-a^2-ab, giving 0 = 2b^2-a^2-ab = -(a+2b)(a-b). For positive quantities a = b, so c = 2b-a = b. Thus a = b = c, and equal numbers are trivially in G.P.: c, a, b are in G.P.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q3(b); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Chain the three means: c^2 = bd with d = 2ce/(c+e) and b = (a+c)/2 collapses to c^2 = ae.
questions.question: Q3(c). If a, b, c are in A.P., b, c, d are in G.P. and c, d, e are in H.P., then prove that a, c, e are in G.P.
questions.solution: b = (a+c)/2, c^2 = bd, and 2/d = 1/c+1/e gives d = 2ce/(c+e). Then c^2 = b·2ce/(c+e) = (a+c)ce/(c+e). So c^2(c+e) = ce(a+c), i.e. c^3+c^2e = ace+c^2e, giving c^3 = ace, so c^2 = ae. Hence a, c, e are in G.P.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q3(c); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: The AP case is (a-c)^2/4 >= 0; the HP case follows by applying the AP case to the reciprocals.
questions.question: Q4. If a, b, c are in A.P., G.P. or H.P., show that b^2 is >, = or < ac respectively.
questions.solution: A.P.: b = (a+c)/2, so b^2-ac = (a+c)^2/4-ac = (a-c)^2/4 >= 0, i.e. b^2 >= ac (> unless a = c). G.P.: b^2 = ac by definition. H.P.: 1/a, 1/b, 1/c are in A.P., so by the A.P. case (1/b)^2 >= (1/a)(1/c), i.e. 1/b^2 >= 1/ac, so b^2 <= ac (< unless a = c).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q4; book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Sum-product with AM = 25, GM = 20: t^2-50t+400 = 0 splits as (t-10)(t-40).
questions.question: Q5(a). The A.M. of two numbers is 25 and their G.M. is 20. Find the numbers.
questions.solution: Let the numbers be a, b. Then a+b = 50 and ab = 20^2 = 400. They are the roots of t^2-50t+400 = 0: t = (50±sqrt(2500-1600))/2 = (50±30)/2, so t = 40 or 10. The numbers are 40 and 10 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q5(a); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: From A-G = 2 and G-H = 1.6 with H = G^2/A: 2G = 1.6(G+2) forces G = 8, A = 10.
questions.question: Q5(b). The difference between the A.M. and G.M. of two numbers is 2, and the difference between the G.M. and the H.M. is 1.6. Find the numbers.
questions.solution: Let G be the G.M.; then A = G+2 and ab = G^2. H = ab/A = G^2/(G+2). G-H = 1.6 gives G-G^2/(G+2) = 1.6, i.e. 2G/(G+2) = 1.6, so 2G = 1.6G+3.2, giving G = 8. Then A = 10, a+b = 20, ab = 64: t^2-20t+64 = 0 gives t = (20±sqrt(400-256))/2 = (20±12)/2, so t = 16 or 4. The numbers are 16 and 4 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q5(b); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: AP sum 36 makes the middle term 12; the GP condition 16^2 = (13-d)(55+d) is a quadratic with roots d = 9, -51.
questions.question: Q6. The sum of three numbers in A.P. is 36. Adding 1, 4 and 43 to them respectively, the resulting numbers are in G.P. Find the numbers.
questions.solution: Let the numbers be 12-d, 12, 12+d (sum 36 forces middle term 12). After adding: 13-d, 16, 55+d in G.P., so 16^2 = (13-d)(55+d) = 715-42d-d^2. Hence d^2+42d-459 = 0, so d = (-42±sqrt(1764+1836))/2 = (-42±60)/2, giving d = 9 or d = -51. For d = 9: 3, 12, 21. For d = -51: 63, 12, -39. (Matches the printed key, whose '6. a)' line has no 6(b) — filed as a label slip.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q6; book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Take logs with x = G/r: the lny terms sum to zero and the lnr coefficient is a+c-2b = 0.
questions.question: Q7(a). If a^x = b^y = c^z and a, b, c are in G.P., prove that x, y, z are in H.P.
questions.solution: Put a^x = b^y = c^z = k. Then x = lnk/lna, y = lnk/lnb, z = lnk/lnc. Since a, b, c are in G.P., lnb-lna = lnc-lnb. Now 1/x+1/z-2/y = (lna+lnc-2lnb)/lnk = 0, so 2/y = 1/x+1/z: x, y, z are in H.P.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q7(a); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Two AMs split [a,b] in thirds: 2p-q = a and 2q-p = b recover the endpoints, whose product is G^2.
questions.question: Q7(b). If one G.M. G and two A.M.s p and q are inserted between two given positive numbers, prove that G^2 = (2p-q)(2q-p).
questions.solution: Let the numbers be a, b. Then G^2 = ab, p = a+(b-a)/3 = (2a+b)/3, q = a+2(b-a)/3 = (a+2b)/3. Now 2p-q = (4a+2b-a-2b)/3 = a and 2q-p = (2a+4b-2a-b)/3 = b. So (2p-q)(2q-p) = ab = G^2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q7(b); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Reciprocate: (b+c)/bc = 1/b+1/c; with 1/a,1/b,1/c as u,u+d,u+2d the three sums are 2u+3d,2u+2d,2u+d.
questions.question: Q8(i). If a, b, c are in H.P., prove that bc/(b+c), ca/(c+a), ab/(a+b) are in H.P.
questions.solution: (i) The reciprocals are (b+c)/bc = 1/b+1/c, 1/c+1/a, 1/a+1/b. Since 1/a, 1/b, 1/c are in A.P. (say u, u+d, u+2d), these sums are 2u+3d, 2u+2d, 2u+d — in A.P. — so the originals are in H.P.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q8(i); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Expand (2a-b)(2c-b) and use 2ac = b(a+c) from the HP condition: everything cancels to b^2.
questions.question: Q8(ii). If a, b, c are in H.P., prove that 2a-b, b, 2c-b are in G.P.
questions.solution: (2a-b)(2c-b) = 4ac-2b(a+c)+b^2. From the H.P. condition 1/a+1/c = 2/b we get 2ac = b(a+c). Substituting: 4ac-4ac+b^2 = b^2. So (2a-b)(2c-b) = b^2: the three are in G.P.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q8(ii); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Successive differences are c(b-a) and a(c-b): equal iff ab+bc = 2ac, the HP condition.
questions.question: Q8(iii). If a, b, c are in H.P., prove that a(b+c), b(c+a), c(a+b) are in A.P.
questions.solution: Second minus first: b(c+a)-a(b+c) = c(b-a). Third minus second: c(a+b)-b(c+a) = a(c-b). Equality needs c(b-a) = a(c-b), i.e. ab+bc = 2ac, i.e. 1/c+1/a = 2/b, exactly the H.P. condition. So the three are in A.P.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.1 Q8(iii); book p215 = PDF p242 (vision read)
